title: Enhance CI backcompat and introduce dependency-curation adapter
author: Iris Monroe
release_notes: Add backwards-compatible CI adapters and a dependency curation shim. No breaking changes to user-facing APIs. Improves presubmit stability and adds a lightweight release smoke check. Teams may opt into staged rollout in release automation.
description: Context: Our presubmit and release pipelines have accumulated several ad-hoc shims to support older runner images and nonstandard team setups. This has led to flaky lint/test runs and unpredictable dependency rollouts. Motivation: reduce flakiness, make CI updates incremental and reversible, and give teams a lightweight path to adopt new policies. Summary: this PR introduces a two-part change: (1) a CI backcompat adapter that injects minimal env and tooling shims for older runners (debounced and opt-in by team via pipeline config); (2) a dependency-curation adapter (dep-fence) that quarantines transitive updates flagged as high-risk and routes them through a curated presubmit job. Key changes: - split the monolithic "lint-runner" into language adapters (js, py, go) with a small common shim; adapters are feature-flagged so rollout is gradual - add a lightweight release-smoke job that runs after gated merges to validate a short end-to-end invocation against staging (fast, ~30s) - introduce dep-curation adapter which tags certain transitive updates (package heuristics + vulnerability signals) and gates them to a curated queue with stricter presubmit checks - provide migration helpers: scripts that detect team configs that need the backcompat shim and a dry-run mode for admins - docs and quickstart examples for adopting the new adapters Checklist: - [x] Implement backcompat adapter and shim - [x] Break out lint language adapters and tests - [x] Implement dep-curation heuristics and quarantine queue - [x] Add release-smoke job and wiring into release automation - [x] Add migration script and docs - [x] Add e2e smoke tests for staged rollout - [x] Run internal canary on infra repo Design notes: Backcompat adapter is intentionally minimal: it only supplies environment variables, wraps a small set of preflight commands, and gracefully passes through unknown args. The dep-curation adapter operates as a lightweight filter: it tags PRs with a bot label and moves them into a separate presubmit lane; maintainers can review and promote to the regular merge queue. Rollout plan: land this PR behind feature-flag, enable adapters for a single team (infra) for 48h, monitor presubmit pass rate and rerun flakiness metric, then enable org-wide in staged waves. Migration: run scripts/tools/migrate-ci-config.sh --dry-run to list impacted repos and suggested config changes. Testing: unit tests for adapters added under infra/ci/adapters, presubmit smoke harness updated; manual smoke run performed against infra-canary. Risks & mitigations: Risk: adapter misses an edge-case runner environment -> mitigated by conservative defaults and opt-in flag. Risk: dep quarantine increases PR feedback latency -> mitigated by curated queue SLA and automatic fast-path for small patch bump PRs. Links: Linear ENG-1942 for rollout plan, ENG-1987 for dep curation heuristics.

notes: This PR touches CI infra only. If teams observe unexpected presubmit failures after the staged rollout, run scripts/migrate-ci-config.sh --rollback <repo> to revert to previous pipeline config. Ops: monitor 'presubmit/pass_rate' and 'presubmit/median_run_time' dashboards for 72 hours post-rollout.
